Opening paragraph: what this animal is, in plain language, for someone who has never taken invertebrate zoology. Two or three sentences.

## 1. Who they are

Taxonomy in one short paragraph — enough to place the group on the tree in the [section overview](index.qmd), not a full classification.

Then the species the lab actually touches, as a short list with why each one matters.

## 2. Body plan

Anatomy oriented around what gets dissected and sampled, not around a textbook tour. If a structure never appears in a lab protocol, it probably does not need a paragraph.

Name the tissues that show up in sample metadata and explain what each one does.

## 3. Life cycle

Spawning through settlement, with the developmental windows the lab's exposure experiments target called out explicitly.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["stage"] --> B["stage"] --> C["stage"]
```

## 4. Physiology essentials

Feeding, respiration, circulation, calcification, immunity. Keep each to a short paragraph — depth belongs in the reading list.

## 5. Why the lab cares

The applied and conceptual hooks: aquaculture, ocean acidification, disease, environmental memory. Link into [the framework](../framework/conceptual-framework.qmd) where the connection is direct.

## 6. Genomic resources

Reference assemblies with accessions, and where they live (NCBI, Ensembl Metazoa, Echinobase, ReefGenomics). Link back to the [technical modules](../modules/04-blast.qmd) that use them.
